reading.rtitle: Five Rules for the Last Meeting
paras: The last meeting of a deal is short, but it is the most important one. The documents are ready, the lawyers are tired, and everybody wants to sign. This is exactly the moment when people make expensive mistakes.

Rule one: know your bottom line before you enter the room. If you did not know it, you would accept anything at the end. Rule two: do not give a concession for free. Ask for something back: 'If we accepted your price, would you pay thirty percent upfront?'

Rule three: find the real deal-breaker. Most problems are small, and you can meet halfway. Rule four: be ready to walk away. If the other side knew you would never leave, they would ask for more and more. Rule five: put everything in writing. A term sheet with the main points is better than a handshake.
Experienced negotiators say the same thing: the best deals are not the ones where one side wins everything. They are the ones that both sides would sign again tomorrow.

listenings.text: Hi, Rafael, it is Claire. Before tomorrow's meeting, I want to be honest with you. My client likes the deal, but the price is a problem. If you lowered it by ten percent, I think we would sign tomorrow. We could also be flexible on the payment. For example, we could pay forty percent upfront and the rest in twelve months. The delivery date is not a deal-breaker for us. Please think about it, and call me tonight if you can.

I have closed more than two hundred deals, and the last meeting always feels the same. Everybody is tired, and everybody wants to finish. My advice is simple. Before the meeting, write your bottom line on a piece of paper, and do not change it in the room. If the other side asks for a concession, ask for one back. And remember that walking away is also a result. If I had to choose between a bad deal and no deal, I would choose no deal every time. But most of the time, if both sides meet halfway, the deal closes, and everybody goes home happy.

extra_audio.text: First, thank the other side and confirm the main points. Then, say your bottom line. Next, make an offer with if and would. After that, meet halfway on the small problems. Finally, put everything in a term sheet and close the deal.
